title: Fake parade bands and the fight with the union boss
summary: Lala explains how he padded parade bands with non-playing men in uniforms, with Emile Gonzales on drums, until Benny Morris made him stop.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: I used to have fights, advertised fights. But only six men in a way, six men, you know? In Italian, in the foiniture wagon, it's an old-time foiniture wagon. Hell, when I got two, I had a 60-man there playing the parade, all, just to go and see the fight. I was playing the marailles, I didn't care. I was playing the parades here, when the time of the parades, the parades used to break up in the French opera, and I suppose you had 12 men in there. The Green, Yellow, Nunes, Bill Jaloti, and who else? I can't think now. I'm trying to think. About five or six good men, all the rest dumbass. We should give you uniform and instruments. Now, you keep it when we're playing, put it by your mouth. Because at least you collect the money, see? We had 12 men, we had six good men in all dumbass, you know? We had two, Gonzales playing drums, Emile Gonzales, and who had, old man, some bass drum band, they had them playing drums. And we had two bands, one was here and one in the front. And the one in the back, he had six dumbass, I had six dumbass. I told him to play, they'd run up and play with me, the good man, you know? See? So the fella told Benny Morris about it, Benny Morris caught me on Burberry Street. He said, what's the matter with that man named Flayne? I said, he's got two legs. I said, what's the matter with that guy? I said, his feet, what? He said, what the hell do you got to do with him playing? So he called me in the office and I had to cut it out. I had to cut it out. I had to get you to collect all that money. I remember the slang he used to do. I had to do that. We used to have moot, dumbass, man. Get him with a uniform, a cap, and the instrument in your hand. You know? I'm already walking in and making a different band. We used to show him how the whole instrument playing. He said, don't blow nothing, for God's sake. Oh, the time gets to heaven.
